CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). (4) The AgentDriver-vs-OperatorGateway distinction recorded here is PRESERVED and now realised: the SDK adapter is the agent-facing side, and the OperatorGateway (event envelopes, hydration/reconnect, first-responder arbitration, WebSocket backpressure) is the operator-facing side.
